subject: Supply Chain & Logistics
title: Railroads Transform Trade
description: A fast breakdown of Railroads Transform Trade for builders.

hook.text: Before railroads, moving goods 30 miles inland cost as much as shipping them across the Atlantic.

buildup.text: Railroads made overland transport fast and cheap for the first time. Goods moved hundreds of miles in a day.

discovery.text: They opened interior markets, connected farms to cities, and enabled factories to source from far away.

twist.text: Railroads required standard time zones. Before trains, every city set its own clock.

climax.text: The US transcontinental railroad in 1869 cut coast-to-coast travel from six months to six days.

punchline.text: Railroads didn't just move goods. They shrank the map.

quiz.question: What did railroads force the creation of?
